title: The city you recognize
hook: Can recognizing one city help when you cannot compare their populations?

knows: basic arithmetic and reading a small table
doesNotKnow: Specify when a recognition heuristic can exploit informative environmental structure.

misconception: The quantities in this case can be combined without checking their reference, denominator, or information boundary.
objective: Specify when a recognition heuristic can exploit informative environmental structure.
keyState: Both complete computed cases are visible as retained observations; the question-case picture survives Reset.

claims.text: A toy recognition cue is correct 80% of the time over ten questions. What is its expected number correct? Toy inputs A=[10, 0.8]; B=[10, 0.5].
claims.source: Local explicit hypothetical assumptions in spec.ts and model.ts; not participant measurements.

claims.text: Computed results: [[8, 1.9999999999999996, 80], [5, 5, 50]]. Labels: Expected right, Expected wrong, Accuracy %.
claims.source: compute() in the lesson-local model.ts; finite numeric operations over the explicit inputs.

claims.text: A recognition cue is useful only under an informative relationship between recognition and the target. The comparison removes that advantage. Expected accuracy is not a guaranteed score, and recognition need not be informative in every environment.
claims.source: The two controlled cases in spec.ts; scope limited to these toy inputs and displayed model rule.

claims.text: A new toy case uses Questions=10, Recognition accuracy=0.5. What is Expected right? Answer: 5.
claims.source: compute() applied to the contrasting new input case; source list is an idea pointer only.

recall.question: A new toy case uses Questions=10, Recognition accuracy=0.5. What is Expected right?
recall.why: Applying the stated toy rule to the new inputs gives 5. The result depends on these assumptions; it is not a universal behavioral response.

sourceProvenance.text: German students guessed which US city was larger better than Americans, by picking the one they recognized (Goldstein & Gigerenzer, 2002).
sourceProvenance.caveat: Original list says figures are approximate and papers were not individually rechecked. No empirical source is verified by this build.

meaningfulDifference: Specify when a recognition heuristic can exploit informative environmental structure.
